headline: For a euro investor, Gradient’s assumptions imply a 30% dollar hedge is most efficient
takeaway: Why: unhedged, a euro investor keeps the 1.55 pp by which Gradient’s dollar cash rate (3.21%) exceeds the euro rate (1.66%), less the 0.91% a year the dollar is assumed to lose. The dollar is also assumed to rise when equities fall (correlation −0.25), offsetting some risk. The first 30% of hedge removes more currency volatility than return; beyond that, the lost carry dominates.
